questions.q: A group of market women in Aba campaigns for higher market levies to be reduced and for better sanitation facilities, but it does not field candidates in council elections. The group is best classified as a
options: political party
pressure group
electoral commission
local government council
questions.explanation: The group seeks to influence public policy without contesting elections, which is the mark of a pressure group. A political party would sponsor candidates, while a local government council and an electoral commission are government bodies.

questions.q: A politician in Kano spends ₦2,000,000 on cash gifts for delegates during a party primary. This practice is most likely to
options: weaken internal democracy within the party
promote equality among party members
increase genuine popular participation in candidate selection
strengthen the rule of law in party administration
questions.explanation: Using money to influence delegates distorts free choice in party primaries and allows wealthy politicians to capture party structures, thereby weakening internal democracy. Such gifts do not promote equality or genuine participation; they give undue advantage to wealthy contestants.

questions.q: A constitution contained in a single document that can be amended by a simple majority in the legislature is best described as
options: written and flexible
written and rigid
unwritten and flexible
unwritten and rigid
questions.explanation: Being contained in one document makes the constitution written, while amendment by simple majority makes it flexible. A rigid constitution requires a special or more demanding amendment procedure.

questions.q: The entrenchment of fundamental human rights in the Nigerian Constitution is principally intended to
options: make the judiciary dependent on the executive
remove all restrictions on individual freedom
limit the misuse of governmental authority over citizens
transfer legislative power to the courts
questions.explanation: Entrenched rights place limits on what the state may do to individuals and provide grounds for redress in court. They do not create absolute freedom without lawful limits or transfer legislative responsibilities to judges.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the ECOWAS Protocol on Free Movement of Persons, Residence and Establishment?
options: To create a single military command for member states
To allow citizens of member states to enter, reside and work in one another's territories under established conditions
To replace national currencies with a common West African currency
To make the ECOWAS Court the final court of appeal for all member states
questions.explanation: The Protocol aims to ease movement and settlement of Community citizens across member states, subject to valid travel documents and immigration conditions. It does not create a joint army command, replace national courts, or introduce a single currency.

questions.q: In Nigeria's presidential system, the main responsibility for preparing and presenting the annual budget to the National Assembly lies with the
options: Auditor-General for the Federation
President of the Senate
President
Chief Justice of Nigeria
questions.explanation: The executive prepares the budget estimates and the President presents them to the National Assembly for consideration and approval. The Auditor-General audits public accounts, while the presiding officers and Chief Justice do not prepare the budget.

questions.q: Nigeria’s decision to send relief materials to victims of a flood in a neighbouring West African country best illustrates the policy of
options: economic nationalism
collective security
non-alignment
good neighbourliness
questions.explanation: Good neighbourliness involves friendly relations, including humanitarian assistance, toward neighbouring states. Non-alignment concerns Cold War alliances, collective security concerns joint defence, and economic nationalism concerns protecting the national economy.

questions.q: A system of government in which religious leaders rule according to religious law is best described as
options: autocracy
theocracy
aristocracy
plutocracy
questions.explanation: Theocracy is rule by religious leaders and religious law. Autocracy is unrestricted rule by one person, plutocracy is rule by the wealthy, and aristocracy is rule by a privileged elite.

questions.q: A government may be said to enjoy legitimacy when its citizens
options: receive development assistance from foreign donors
obey its orders only because of fear of punishment
accept its right to rule and obey its laws willingly
conduct elections at regular intervals
questions.explanation: Legitimacy exists when citizens accept that the government has the right to rule. Obedience based only on fear indicates coercion rather than legitimacy. Regular elections or foreign aid may help but do not by themselves prove that citizens accept the government's right to rule.

questions.q: A civil servant in Abuja carries out an order from the Director of Finance because the order is supported by written regulations and the office the director occupies. This obedience best illustrates
options: charismatic authority
traditional authority
coercive power
legal-rational authority
questions.explanation: Legal-rational authority rests on rules, laws and the official positions people occupy. Traditional authority rests on inherited custom, while charismatic authority rests on personal qualities. Coercive power works through force or threats rather than accepted rules.

questions.q: Where no political party wins an outright majority in parliament, two or more parties may agree to form a government. This arrangement is known as
options: a caucus
a referendum
a coalition
an opposition
questions.explanation: A coalition is an alliance of two or more parties who combine to form a government or secure a majority. An opposition refers to parties outside the government, while a referendum is a direct vote by the electorate. A caucus is usually a meeting or bloc within a party or legislature.

questions.q: A professional association in Lagos holds press conferences, submits memoranda to the National Assembly and meets lawmakers privately in order to shape a proposed law. These activities are examples of
options: electioneering
gerrymandering
lobbying
judicial review
questions.explanation: Lobbying is the organized effort to influence legislators and public policy, often through meetings, memoranda and public campaigns. Electioneering is campaigning for votes, while gerrymandering is the manipulation of electoral boundaries. Judicial review is the court's power to examine the legality of laws or actions.

questions.q: In a certain country, the powers of the prime minister are found partly in Acts of Parliament, partly in court decisions and partly in long-standing practices not written in one document. That country is said to have
options: an unwritten constitution
a rigid constitution
a written constitution
a federal constitution
questions.explanation: An unwritten constitution is not contained in a single document but is found in statutes, judicial decisions and conventions. Rigidity concerns the amendment procedure, while federalism concerns the division of powers between central and component units. The key fact here is that the rules are not gathered into one written document.

questions.q: One reason the Nigerian Constitution is regarded as rigid is that
options: its amendment requires special majorities and approval by state legislatures
it is contained in a single document
it divides powers between the federal and state governments
it contains a preamble and fundamental rights
questions.explanation: A rigid constitution can be amended only through a special procedure, not by ordinary legislation. In Nigeria, amendment involves special majorities in the National Assembly and approval by the required number of state legislatures. A preamble, a bill of rights or a federal division of powers does not by itself make a constitution rigid.

questions.q: Nigeria and a neighbouring state agree to refer a boundary dispute to the International Court of Justice. The Court hears the case mainly because it is
options: the principal judicial organ of the United Nations
an organ of ECOWAS
a peacekeeping force of the Security Council
a specialised agency for boundary disputes
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations and settles legal disputes submitted to it by states. It is not a peacekeeping force, a specialised agency, or an ECOWAS institution. Its role is judicial rather than military or purely regional.

questions.q: A trader from Kano sells made-in-Nigeria goods in Accra without paying import duty under an ECOWAS arrangement. This benefit is provided mainly by ECOWAS's policy of
options: political integration
collective security
a common currency
trade liberalisation
questions.explanation: ECOWAS promotes trade liberalisation by reducing tariff and non-tariff barriers among member states. A common currency is still a planned objective rather than an existing arrangement, and collective security concerns defence. Political integration is broader and does not directly explain duty-free trading in goods.

questions.q: Musa, a trader detained at a police station in Kano for more than the period allowed by law, applies to the High Court for an order that he be brought before the court so that the lawfulness of his detention may be examined. The order being sought is a writ of
options: prohibition
habeas corpus
mandamus
certiorari
questions.explanation: Habeas corpus commands that a person in detention be brought before the court for inquiry into the legality of the detention. Mandamus compels a public officer to perform a duty, while certiorari is used to quash a decision and prohibition restrains a tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the Speaker of a State House of Assembly may be removed from office by
options: a simple majority vote of the House on a motion moved by the Governor
a directive of the State Executive Council approved by the Governor
a resolution of the House supported by not less than two-thirds majority of its members
an order of the Chief Judge of the State
questions.explanation: Removal of the Speaker or Deputy Speaker is by a resolution of the House supported by not less than a two-thirds majority, after a notice signed by at least one-third of members. A governor's directive or a Chief Judge's order cannot remove the Speaker, and a simple majority is insufficient.

questions.q: In Nigeria, the prerogative of mercy in respect of a person convicted by a state High Court is exercised by the
options: Governor, acting on the advice of the State Advisory Council on the Prerogative of Mercy
Chief Judge of the state sitting alone
Speaker of the State House of Assembly on a resolution of the House
State Attorney-General after reviewing the case file
questions.explanation: The Constitution vests the prerogative of mercy in the Governor, who acts on the advice of the State Advisory Council on the Prerogative of Mercy. The Chief Judge and the Attorney-General may advise or administer aspects of justice, but they do not exercise this power personally, and the Speaker does not grant pardons.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The requirement that the President obtain the approval of the National Assembly before borrowing money on behalf of the Federation is best described as
options: judicial review of administrative action
executive control over the legislature
an aspect of local government autonomy
a legislative check on the financial powers of the executive
questions.explanation: The Constitution makes borrowing by the Federation subject to legislative approval, thereby allowing the National Assembly to check executive financial power. It is not executive control, judicial review, or a local government matter.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: Which situation most directly violates the principle of checks and balances in a presidential system of government?
options: A President orders the detention of judges who give judgments against his administration
The Senate rejects a presidential nominee for a ministerial appointment
The National Assembly overrides a presidential veto by the required majority
The Supreme Court nullifies a law that conflicts with the Constitution
questions.explanation: Detaining judges for their rulings attacks judicial independence and removes the judiciary's ability to check the executive. Rejection of a nominee, judicial nullification of an unconstitutional law and a legislative override of a veto are themselves normal checks and balances.

questions.q: The concentric circles approach to Nigeria’s foreign policy places the greatest priority on
options: participation in the United Nations system
ties with the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
co-operation with the Commonwealth of Nations
relations with her immediate neighbours and the West African sub-region
questions.explanation: The concentric circles doctrine starts from the immediate neighbourhood and West Africa, then extends to Africa and the wider world. The Commonwealth, OIC and UN are important, but they fall outside the innermost circle in this framework.

questions.q: After the execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa and other Ogoni activists in 1995, Nigeria’s relations with many Western countries were strained mainly because the government of General Sani Abacha was accused of
options: withdrawing from the Commonwealth
serious human rights abuses
refusing to pay its United Nations dues
banning all crude oil exports
questions.explanation: The execution attracted international condemnation and led to measures such as Nigeria's suspension from the Commonwealth, with the Abacha government criticised for human rights violations. Non-payment of UN dues, an oil export ban and withdrawal from the Commonwealth were not the cause of that crisis.

questions.q: The 1914 amalgamation of the Northern and Southern Protectorates by Lord Lugard is important in Nigeria’s constitutional development because it
options: brought the two territories under a single colonial administration
created the first elected legislature for the whole country
introduced a federal system of government in Nigeria
granted universal adult suffrage to Nigerians
questions.explanation: The amalgamation united the administration of the Northern and Southern Protectorates under one colonial government, which laid the basis for a single Nigerian state. It did not introduce federalism, an elected national legislature, or universal adult suffrage.

questions.q: Under the Clifford Constitution of 1922, the elective principle was introduced in Lagos and Calabar, but the franchise was restricted mainly to
options: all adult residents of the two towns
adult male taxpayers who met specified property or income qualifications
women who were registered as traders
traditional rulers and their appointed representatives
questions.explanation: The elective principle under the Clifford Constitution was limited, with the right to vote based on adult male status plus property or income qualifications in the designated areas. It was not universal adult suffrage, did not extend the vote to women on the stated basis, and was not confined to traditional rulers.

questions.q: Which feature best distinguishes a republic from a constitutional monarchy?
options: The judiciary is independent of the executive.
The head of state is elected and holds office for a defined tenure.
The legislature is made up of two chambers.
The armed forces are under civilian control.
questions.explanation: In a republic, the head of state is elected or constitutionally chosen for a defined tenure instead of inheriting the office. Bicameral legislatures, independent courts and civilian control can exist under both republics and constitutional monarchies.

questions.q: The principle of collective responsibility is most closely associated with which form of government?
options: Parliamentary system
Confederal system
Military junta
Presidential system
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the cabinet stands or falls together and is answerable to the legislature. A presidential cabinet is individually responsible to the president and not subject to the same collective confidence rule.

questions.q: The division of powers between the federal and state governments in Nigeria is principally intended to
options: make all laws uniform throughout the country
ensure that the federal government controls all local affairs
enable the states to conduct independent foreign policy
prevent excessive concentration of power and accommodate regional diversity
questions.explanation: A federal arrangement shares power between central and regional governments to prevent excessive concentration and accommodate diversity. Nigerian states do not conduct independent foreign policy, and federalism does not require all laws to be uniform.

questions.q: Which of the following is recognised as the third tier of government in Nigeria?
options: Federal Executive Council
Local government council
Council of State
State House of Assembly
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution provides for federal, state and local government councils, and local government councils are described as the third tier. The listed bodies are organs or councils within the federal or state structure, not separate tiers of government.

questions.q: During military rule in Nigeria, a state military governor was primarily responsible for
options: commanding the armed forces at the federal level
overseeing the state judiciary as its chief judge
conducting independent foreign relations for the state
administering the state on behalf of the federal military government
questions.explanation: Military governors were appointed by the federal military government to administer states. They did not conduct independent foreign relations or serve as chief judges; overall command of the armed forces rested with the federal military leadership.

questions.q: The 1979 Constitution was important in Nigeria's transition from military rule because it
options: provided for an elected president and legislatures under a new civilian order
empowered the military to rule indefinitely through decrees
abolished the federal system and created a unitary state
introduced a one-party system for the Second Republic
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution established a presidential system with an elected president and national and state legislatures, preparing the ground for civilian rule. It did not create a unitary or one-party state, nor did it authorize indefinite military rule.

questions.q: A civic group in Kaduna wants to measure residents' opinion on a proposed water tariff. Which method is most likely to produce a representative result?
options: Selecting respondents randomly from different parts of the city
Questioning only the staff of the water agency
Interviewing only members of the civic group
Recording only opinions of callers to a radio phone-in programme
questions.explanation: A random sample drawn from different parts of the city is more likely to reflect the views of the wider population. Interviewing only group members, radio callers, or water agency staff would introduce bias.

questions.q: The principle that all adult citizens who meet the legal requirements should have the right to vote is called...
options: universal adult suffrage
single-member constituency
proportional representation
secret ballot
questions.explanation: Universal adult suffrage means that the right to vote is extended to all adult citizens, subject only to legal qualifications. Proportional representation and single-member constituencies concern how seats are allocated, while the secret ballot concerns how voting is conducted.

questions.q: The main function of an election petition tribunal in Nigeria is to...
options: organise and supervise party primaries
register voters for future elections
review constituency boundaries before elections
hear and determine complaints about the validity of election results
questions.explanation: An election petition tribunal is set up to adjudicate disputes arising from the conduct and results of elections. It does not organise party primaries, register voters, or carry out constituency delimitation, which are different responsibilities.

questions.q: When a member of a State House of Assembly dies before the end of the term, a bye-election is held mainly to...
options: fill the vacant legislative seat
elect a new state governor
approve the annual budget of the state
register members of political parties in the constituency
questions.explanation: A bye-election is conducted to fill a legislative or other elective vacancy that arises between general elections. It is not used to elect a governor, approve a budget, or register party members.

questions.q: The principle of constitutional supremacy means that...
options: the judiciary may amend the constitution by simple majority
the legislature has the final authority to interpret the constitution
the executive may suspend constitutional provisions at will
any law or government action inconsistent with the constitution is invalid
questions.explanation: Constitutional supremacy places the constitution above all other laws and government actions, so inconsistent laws or actions are void to the extent of the inconsistency. The legislature does not interpret the constitution finally, the judiciary does not amend it by simple majority, and the executive cannot suspend its provisions at will.

questions.q: In a federal constitution, residual powers are those powers that are...
options: left to the component states or units
exclusively reserved for the central government
shared concurrently by the central government and the states
exercised only by local government councils
questions.explanation: Residual powers are the matters not assigned to the central government or listed as concurrent, and they remain with the states or component units. Exclusive powers belong to the central government, concurrent powers are shared, and local councils exercise powers given by higher levels.

questions.q: A major limitation to the effectiveness of pressure groups in Nigeria is that they...
options: must contest elections before they can meet government officials
often lack adequate funds and organisation for sustained influence
are usually funded and directed by the Independent National Electoral Commission
are prohibited by the constitution from seeking policy changes
questions.explanation: Many pressure groups in Nigeria are constrained by limited finance, weak organisation, and dependence on members' subscriptions, which reduces their sustained influence on policy. The constitution does not prohibit them from seeking policy changes, they need not contest elections to meet officials, and INEC does not fund or direct them.

questions.q: A community in Oyo State obeys its traditional ruler because the position has been accepted from generation to generation. The ruler's authority is best described as...
options: coercive authority
traditional authority
legal-rational authority
charismatic authority
questions.explanation: Authority based on long-established custom and inherited position is traditional authority. Charismatic authority rests on personal qualities, legal-rational authority rests on laws and office, and coercive authority rests on force or punishment.

questions.q: De jure sovereignty is best defined as the...
options: authority exercised by a traditional ruler over his subjects
actual control of state institutions by a government
legal right of a state to exercise supreme authority over its territory
recognition granted to a state by foreign powers
questions.explanation: De jure sovereignty refers to lawful or rightful supreme authority, whether or not it is fully effective in practice. Actual control refers to de facto sovereignty, foreign recognition is a form of international recognition, and traditional rulership is a different kind of authority.

questions.q: The New Partnership for Africa's Development (NEPAD) was adopted by the African Union mainly to
options: settle boundary disputes between African states
promote socio-economic development and good governance in Africa
train a joint continental army for peace enforcement
coordinate a common African currency for all member states
questions.explanation: NEPAD is a development framework designed to encourage economic growth, poverty reduction, and good governance in Africa. It is not a currency union arrangement, a boundary dispute court, or a continental army programme.

questions.q: The Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) of the United Nations is chiefly responsible for
options: commanding UN peacekeeping operations in conflict zones
settling legal disputes between member states
coordinating the economic, social and related work of the UN and its specialised agencies
admitting new member states into the United Nations
questions.explanation: ECOSOC coordinates the economic, social, and related activities of the United Nations and its specialised agencies. Admission of new members is handled by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council, while legal disputes between states may go to the International Court of Justice.

questions.q: In the Nigerian National Assembly, a public bill is one which
options: is introduced by a private citizen without the consent of the legislature
originates from a state House of Assembly
deals with matters affecting the general public
affects only a particular individual or local interest
questions.explanation: A public bill concerns matters of general public importance, such as education, taxation, or public order. A bill that affects only a particular individual, family, or local interest is classified as a private bill, not a public bill.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The confirmation of ministerial nominees by the Senate is best described as
options: an executive check on the legislature
a legislative check on the executive
a judicial review of executive action
a function of the Council of State
questions.explanation: The Senate is part of the legislature, and its power to confirm ministerial nominees enables it to check the President's appointment powers. This is not an executive check, a judicial review, or a Council of State function, since the Council of State merely advises the President.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the promotion of African integration and support for African unity is contained in the chapter dealing with
options: Code of Conduct for public officers
citizenship and fundamental rights
fundamental objectives and directive principles of state policy
powers of the National Assembly
questions.explanation: The foreign policy objectives, including the promotion of African integration and African unity, are stated in Chapter II of the 1999 Constitution under the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy. They are not located in the provisions on citizenship, fundamental rights, legislative powers, or the Code of Conduct.

questions.q: The Richards Constitution of 1946 was criticised mainly because it
options: made Lagos the capital territory of Nigeria
gave women in the North the right to vote
was introduced without adequate consultation with Nigerian leaders
abolished the office of the Governor-General
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution was prepared by the colonial authorities with little consultation of Nigerian political leaders, and this became a major ground of nationalist criticism. The other claims do not describe its provisions; for instance, it did not abolish the office of the Governor.

questions.q: A major constitutional change introduced by the Lyttelton Constitution of 1954 was the
options: division of powers between the central government and the regions
establishment of a single legislative council for the whole country
creation of the office of the Prime Minister for Nigeria
introduction of the elective principle in Lagos and Calabar
questions.explanation: The Lyttelton Constitution strengthened federal arrangements by distributing legislative powers between the central government and the regions. The elective principle was introduced earlier under the Clifford Constitution, while the office of Prime Minister came later.

questions.q: In a parliamentary system of government, the ministers are usually
options: members of the legislature from which they are drawn
selected by the head of state from outside the legislature only
elected directly by the people in separate executive elections
appointed by the judiciary to supervise laws
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system the executive is drawn from and remains responsible to the legislature, so ministers normally sit in Parliament. Direct separate election of the executive is characteristic of a presidential system, not a parliamentary one.

questions.q: A major criticism of the presidential system of government is that it may lead to
options: deadlock between the executive and the legislature when controlled by different parties
excessive dependence of the executive on parliamentary confidence
absence of a fixed term for the president
rapid fusion of executive and legislative powers
questions.explanation: Because the President and the legislature are separately elected and have fixed terms, divided party control can produce conflict and delay. A parliamentary system, by contrast, normally relies on the executive retaining the confidence of the legislature.

questions.q: The major reason for adopting a federal system in Nigeria was to
options: make the judiciary subordinate to the executive
ensure that only one political party operates in the country
concentrate all legislative powers in the centre
accommodate the country's ethnic and regional diversity
questions.explanation: Federalism was chosen to allow the various ethnic and regional groups to share power while preserving some autonomy for component units. A unitary arrangement concentrating all powers at the centre would not address this concern.
